editorial:
You walk into a rainy courtyard where four people tell four different stories about one murder and one assault. A bandit, a samurai, his wife, and a woodcutter each remember the forest scene in their own way, and every version makes you question who is telling the truth. The black-and-white images, heavy rain, and tense courtroom mood pull you in fast, even though the story stays simple and human.

The acting is very bold and memorable, especially the wild bandit and the shaken wife, while the pacing keeps you guessing without rushing. It is a classic, so the old style and subtitles may take a minute to get used to, but the mystery stays very strong. Watch it if you really like crime stories, moral puzzles, or film history.
endingExplained: In the last scenes, the woodcutter finally admits he saw the bandit kill the samurai after the wife ran away, and he also took the valuable dagger. Still, no one knows which story is fully true. The movie ends with the woodcutter taking in an abandoned baby as the rain stops and the sun comes out. That final act gives you a small sign of hope, even though the murder stays a mystery.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves classic mysteries and moral puzzles.
